The answer is B. In a uniform magnetic field, the net force on any closed current loop is zero. The force on a piece of wire is F = I∫dl × B. Because B is the same everywhere, it can be taken outside the integral, and the vectors dl around a closed loop add up to zero. For a rectangle, this means the forces on opposite sides are equal in size and point in opposite directions.

Those paired forces do not act along the same line, though, so they can still twist the loop. The torque is τ = μ × B. This is not zero whenever the field is not perpendicular to the loop's plane, which means the field and the loop's magnetic moment are not lined up.

The phrase "at an angle" is a little loose. If the angle meant was 90° (field perpendicular to the plane), the torque would be zero. The usual reading is an oblique angle, so I'm treating the item as sound.

answers.brief_reasoning: In a uniform field the net force on a closed loop is zero because the integral of dl around the loop is zero. The torque, τ = μ × B, is not zero when the plane of the loop is at an oblique angle to the field.
